claims.text: Under sustained loading, HEA multilayer coatings progressively accommodate plastic deformation through an interface-mediated, dislocation-triggered phase transformation at nanolamellar boundaries.
The deformation-induced transformation can proceed from FCC to HCP.
The transformed phase has lower stacking-fault energy than the initial FCC phase.
A dislocation pile-up at coherent interfaces must reach a critical threshold to activate the phase transformation.
The transformation enables additional deformation modes such as enhanced twinning or slip.
Transformation-assisted deformation maintains strength while improving deformation tolerance.
The proposed starting material is a nanoscale coherent HEA multilayer coating with a single-phase FCC structure and sharp interfaces.
Sustained loading can activate dislocation accumulation while preserving the nanoscale multilayer architecture.
Coherent layer interfaces serve as barriers to dislocation motion.
Coherent layer interfaces serve as nucleation sites for deformation-induced phase transformation.
Dislocation accumulation creates a critical local stress at interfaces that triggers the transformation.
The localized transformation promotes progressive plastic strain accommodation and enhanced work hardening.
The secondary-phase fraction should gradually increase at interfaces and correlate with accumulated plastic strain.
HEA multilayers should show delayed necking and a higher work-hardening rate than conventional multilayers deforming only by dislocation slip.
Plastic deformation in conventional metallic multilayers under sustained loading is dominated by uniform dislocation slip with little or no interfacial phase transformation.
The mechanism requires preservation of the nanoscale multilayer architecture and loading sufficient for interfacial dislocation accumulation but below catastrophic-failure conditions.
Extreme temperatures or composition changes that destabilize interface coherence can invalidate the proposed mechanism.
The hypothesis is falsified if sustained loading produces only uniform slip, no detectable interface-localized transformation, and no work-hardening or ductility improvement relative to the baseline.
